crafts.boondoggle: Flat plastic lace (scoubidou, gimp, lanyard) woven stitch on stitch. Every stitch is an MxN stitch.
crafts.macrame: Cords knotted round each other or round filler cords.
crafts.chinese knotting: Decorative knots tied in one cord, laid flat.
crafts.knitting: Loops of one yarn pulled through the loops of the row below.
crafts.crochet: Loops of one yarn pulled through each other with a hook.
crafts.knots: Rope knots, each with its tying steps.

entries.name: box_stitch
entries.title: Box stitch
entries.about: The basic boondoggle stitch: two strings, four ends, each folded over the next, a 2 by 2 square seen from above. It is the 1x1 MxN stitch.

entries.name: brick_stitch
entries.title: Brick stitch
entries.about: Three strings, six ends: two strings one way and one across, a 2 by 3 rectangle seen from above. It is the 2x1 MxN stitch.

entries.name: mxn_stitch
entries.title: MxN stitch
entries.about: Any boondoggle stitch: m strings one way and n the other, each from 1 to 8, left or right hand, loose or stretched.

entries.name: chinese_cloverleaf
entries.title: Cloverleaf knot
entries.about: Four heart-shaped leaves interlocking on one closed cord, with a stem tucked under the centre. Shown finished and flat; no tying steps yet.

entries.name: good_luck_knot_crowned
entries.title: Good luck knot, tied by crowning
entries.about: The good luck knot as it is taught: the cord folded into a cross of three loops and two ends, then crowned, each arm folded over the next one anticlockwise and the last tucked through the bend of the first. Shown step by step, with arrows: the cross and the first crown drawn by hand, then the crown pulled snug and the second crown, clockwise, on top.

steps.caption: Fold the cord into a cross: a loop at the top, one to the left, one to the right, and the two ends hanging down. The arrows show where each arm folds next, anticlockwise.

Fold the top loop down over the left loop, the left loop over it to the right, and the ends up over the left loop. Fold the right loop over the ends to the left and tuck it through the bend of the top loop, then pull all four arms out to tighten.
Pull the crown snug, leaving the four arms long. Now crown again on top, this time clockwise, as the arrows show.

The second crown lies on top of the first, turned the other way: each arm folds over the next and the last is tucked through the bend of the first. Pull the arms out to tighten, then ease out the three large ears and the four small ones between them.

entries.name: chrysanthemum_knot
entries.title: Chrysanthemum knot
entries.about: The good luck knot with both crowns turned the same way, as Japanese books tie it: the cord laid in a cross of three bights and the two ends, crowned anticlockwise, pulled snug and crowned anticlockwise again on top. It comes out a little less crisp than the good luck knot and hangs slightly differently. Drawn step by step, with arrows.

steps.caption: Lay the cord in a cross: a bight up, one to the left, one to the right, and the two ends down. The arrows show the crown: each arm folds anticlockwise over the next.
Crown: fold each arm anticlockwise over the base of the next, on top of the fold before it, and tuck the last one through the bend of the first. Then pull the four arms out.
Pull the crown snug, leaving the arms long. Now crown again on top, anticlockwise as before.
The second crown lies on top of the first: each arm folds over the next and the last is tucked through the bend of the first. Pull the arms out to tighten and ease the ears until they match.

entries.name: five_sided_good_luck_knot
entries.title: Five-sided good luck knot
entries.about: A good luck knot of five sides: four bights and the two ends laid in a star, crowned anticlockwise, pulled snug and crowned clockwise on top, as the square good luck knot is tied. One of the knot's many variations with more sides. Drawn step by step, with arrows.

steps.caption: Lay the cord in a star of five arms: four bights and the two ends hanging down. The arrows show the crown: each arm folds anticlockwise over the next.
Crown anticlockwise: fold each arm over the base of the next, on top of the fold before it, and tuck the last one through the bend of the first. Then pull the five arms out.
Pull the crown snug, leaving the arms long. Now crown again on top, this time clockwise.
The second crown lies on top of the first, turned the other way: each arm over the next and the last tucked through the bend of the first. Pull the arms out to tighten and ease the ears even.

entries.name: magic_knot
entries.title: Magic knot
entries.about: Joins a new ball of yarn to the old one: each yarn ties an overhand knot round the other. It is the fisherman's knot.

entries.name: crochet_chain_stitch
entries.title: Chain stitch
entries.about: The first stitch of crochet: from a slip knot on the hook, the yarn is taken over the hook and pulled through the loop again and again, and each pull-through adds one loop to a chain that the next rows are worked into.

steps.caption: Start with a slip knot on the hook: the front leg of its loop lies over the hook and the back leg under it, and the working yarn leads away behind the front leg.
Yarn over: take the working yarn under the hook, then over the top and back across the front of the hook, between the loop and the tip.
Catch the yarn in the hook and pull it through the loop: the old loop comes off the hook as one chain, and both legs of the new loop pass over its edge next to the hook and through it.
Repeat the yarn over and the pull-through: each one adds a chain beside the last. The loop on the hook and the slip knot are not counted.

entries.name: knit_stitch
entries.title: Knit stitch
entries.about: The basic stitch of knitting: the right needle goes into the front of the first stitch on the left needle from left to right, the yarn is wrapped round it and pulled through to the front, and the old stitch slips off. Shown English style, the working yarn held at the back.

steps.caption: With the working yarn at the back, put the right needle into the front of the first stitch on the left needle, from left to right: it goes under the front leg of the stitch and over its back leg, and behind the left needle, so the tips cross with the right needle at the back.
Wrap the working yarn round the right needle between the two tips: from the back, under the right needle, then over it.
Draw the wrap back through the stitch with the right needle: the new loop comes up through the old stitch and out over its front leg, and sits on the right needle in front of the work.
Slip the old stitch off the tip of the left needle: it now hangs round the legs of the new stitch, which stays on the right needle. One knit stitch is made.
